bull_bear.body:
- The AESL contracting transfers merchant-tariff, ISTS/ALMM-waiver and market ups/downs (incl. the ~INR 0.50/unit transmission-cost arbitrage) **to AESL**; AGEL keeps predictable long-term returns.
- Continued reinvestment into greenfield + storage; no dividend/buyback (growth-stage IPP).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Transmission/evacuation availability** is the explicit growth governor.
- **Related-party concentration:** near-all merchant/C&I offtake now with sibling AESL (arm's-length/Audit-Committee-approved, but material RPT optics).
- BESS execution at 10 GWh scale unproven; battery-fire risk — mgmt clarified a competitor's incident was a **PCS/IGBT (inverter) fire, not a battery fire**; projects carry standard insurance + Tier-1 OEMs.
- Falling solar tariffs (units +30% vs revenue +29% roughly matched this quarter) — realisation compression on newer vintages.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and leadership-framed; CEO Ashish Khanna fielded most questions and articulated the de-risking rationale clearly. Some specifics deflected ("benchmark rate" rather than exact per-kWh AESL pricing). Battery-storage CEO Rajat Seksaria credible on fire/insurance and unit economics.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Business-model pivot:** from a merchant-tariff/transmission-arbitrage builder to a fixed-return contracted IPP via AESL — materially lower risk, lower upside, cleaner cash flows. The ISTS/ALMM-waiver and INR 0.50/unit transmission arbitrage upside now sits with AESL.
- The read-through of "grid, not panels, is the bottleneck" points straight at **transmission capex (AESL)** as the group's actual growth governor.
- AGEL ≈ India's entire grid-battery base today; first-mover scale advantage but also concentration risk.
- PSP (ex-Chitravathi) is still ~2 years out — storage growth near-term is BESS-led.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Scale and pace: India's largest renewable energy portfolio (19.3 GW operational as of Mar-2026) with 5.1 GW greenfield capacity added in FY26 — cited as the highest greenfield annual capacity expansion globally by any company excluding China.
- Land and transmission lock-in: secures resource-rich land covering nearly 2,50,000 acres and locks in transmission access early, aligning design/engineering/supply chain to commission projects ahead of PPA timelines and deliver better IRRs.
- O&M execution: analytics-based Operations & Maintenance via its Energy Network Operation Centre (ENOC) monitors all plants across 12 states in real time; solar plant availability above 99.2% and EBITDA margins above 90% maintained for five consecutive years.
- Capital management discipline: matches debt tenure to PPA tenure to lower refinancing risk, drawing on a diversified funding pool of domestic banks/financial institutions, international lenders and global/local bond markets.
- Technology edge: uses bifacial and n-type solar PV modules, horizontal single-axis trackers and India's largest 5.2 MW wind turbines to lower the Levelised Cost of Electricity (LCOE).
- Revenue visibility: approximately 78.4% of the portfolio is backed by executed PPAs with sovereign counterparties (SECI, PTC, NTPC, NHPC, State DISCOMs).
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Related-party transaction exposure within the Adani Group ecosystem — The Company's RPT Policy exists specifically to manage 'potential or actual conflicts of interest' arising from transactions with related parties; all RPTs by the Company, and by subsidiaries exceeding their standalone turnover, are routed through Audit Committee review and, for material RPTs, shareholder approval, signalling a structurally significant related-party transaction base tied to the wider Adani Group.
- Global policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions — The MD&A's global economic outlook notes that growth projections hold only as 'risks from policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions persist,' a macro backdrop relevant to a capital-intensive, financing-dependent renewable energy developer with international lenders and bond-market exposure.

business.body: AGEL develops, owns and runs large-scale grid-connected solar, wind, hybrid, Battery Energy Storage Solution (BESS) and pumped-hydro storage plants, delivering renewable power and storage solutions at scale. outlook.body:
- Shifting the operating model from self-execution to a partner-led model by engaging specialised EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) and O&M (Operations and Maintenance) partners, repositioning the internal workforce toward strategic governance and assurance to keep the organisation agile, scalable and resilient.
- Focused on leveraging technology to reduce the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) in pursuit of enabling large-scale adoption of affordable clean energy.
- People strategy centred on building a future-ready, inclusive and responsible workforce by strengthening skills, leadership and digital capabilities (including Agentic AI, robotic process automation and workforce analytics for demand forecasting and optimisation).
- Cadre hiring strategy to build a robust pipeline of young engineering and management talent for cross-functional capability and long-term growth, supported by a Long Term Retention Bonus (LTRB) to retain top talent.
- AGEL has not declared any dividend since incorporation, including for FY 2025-26 — the Board decided, after holistically considering the tremendous growth opportunities the Company is engaged with, that it would be prudent not to recommend a dividend for the year, and the Board also does not propose to transfer any amount to General Reserves, consistent with a reinvestment-led capital allocation philosophy governed by the Dividend Distribution and Shareholder Return Policy under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: AGEL's flagship greenfield build-out is the Khavda Renewable Energy Park (Gujarat), described as the world's largest single-location renewable power plant under development; against a total planned installed capacity of 30 GW at Khavda, about 9.4 GW had been commissioned as of 31 March 2026, with the remaining capacity work-in-progress. Overall operational renewable capacity jumped 35% YoY to 19.3 GW in FY 2025-26 with a greenfield capacity addition of 5.1 GW (1.5x the FY 2024-25 addition), described as the highest greenfield annual capacity expansion globally by any company excluding China; this was achieved on a capex of ` 30,365 crore during the year. In energy storage, AGEL operationalised 1,376 MWh of BESS capacity at Khavda (installed capacity 1,579 MWh), one of the world's largest single-location BESS deployments, and intends to establish 10+ GWh of BESS capacity by March 2027, leveraging its large Khavda land bank. In pumped-hydro storage (PSP), AGEL has three projects with environmental clearance — Chitravathi (500 MW, Andhra Pradesh), Tarali (1,500 MW) and Gandikota (1,000 MW); Chitravathi, AGEL's first hydro PSP, spans 407 acres and is scheduled to be operational by FY 2026-27, generating over 1 TWh annually with about 6.2 hours per cycle. During the year AGEL also secured PPAs for 1,250 MW PSP capacity from Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd and 500 MW PSP capacity from Assam Power Distribution Company Limited, and works with five states toward a target of over 5 GW PSP capacity by 2030, on the path to AGEL's overall 50 GW renewable capacity target by 2030.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Renewables are expected to overtake coal as the top global electricity source in 2026, reaching 36% of global power at 6,000+ TWh from wind and solar alone, framing a structural industry tailwind.
- India's public capital expenditure reached ` 12.2 lakh crore, advancing infrastructure and stimulating manufacturing, construction and energy sectors, with the Union Budget 2026-27 continuing to prioritise energy transition among its priorities.
- The Indian economy's outlook stays positive and stable, with real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 projected between 6.8% and 7.2%, supported by continued government infrastructure spending and rising private-sector investment.

deepdive.thesis: Q1FY27 opened strong (power-supply revenue +29%, EBITDA +33% at a 94% margin, energy sales +30%, 20 GW milestone crossed), but the defining change this quarter is strategic: AGEL is **de-risking its merchant/C&I exposure by contracting essentially all such capacity to sibling Adani Energy Solutions (AESL)** on 25-yr (solar/wind) and 15-yr (battery) fixed-price arm's-length PPAs. AGEL reframes itself as a pure execution/operational-excellence play chasing predictable ~15–16% IRRs, while BESS scales fast (3.5 GWh installed, 10+ GWh targeted this year).

open.item: Q1 FY26 solar CUF was ~28%; management guides ~28% as a conservative full-year figure, with upside as Khavda's share grows.
Run-rate EBITDA for the 15.8 GW capacity is ~INR 13,600 crores for Q1, equating to ~INR 17,000 crores on a yearly basis; gross block ~INR 89,000 crores.
For the FY26 5 GW build, ~95% of capacity is already under various sanctions with debt tie-up done, generally from domestic sources (REC/PFC).
The 600 MW hybrid project (2.41 tariff) is under implementation and expected to be commissioned sometime in FY26.
Greenfield RE capacity add FY27
Cumulative BESS capacity this fiscal
Maiden Chitravathi pumped-storage commissioning
FY27 capex
Run-rate EBITDA by FY27-end
Maiden Chitravathi pumped-storage commissioning
The Adani-TotalEnergies JV holds a 4.5 GW portfolio, of which ~4 GW is operational and 500 MW is to be commissioned within the next six months to one year.
Management flags evacuation/transmission constraints as the key gating factor sizing FY27 capacity additions to 4.5-5.0 GW rather than higher.
AGEL targets storage capacity of 10+ GWh by March 2027.
AGEL's first hydro pumped-hydro storage project (500 MW), on the Chitravathi River in Andhra Pradesh, is scheduled to be operational in FY 2026-27, generating over 1 TWh annually.
The intent is to establish 10+ GWh of BESS capacity by March 2027, with AGEL's large land bank at Khavda as a key enabler.
AGEL added 1.4 GWh of battery capacity at Khavda in FY26 and plans to reach 10 GWh of storage capacity at Khavda by the end of this fiscal year (FY27), from ~3 GWh currently.
For FY27, AGEL plans to add 4.5 to 5.0 GW of solar and wind capacity, subject to evacuation availability.
AGEL is slated to complete its maiden 500 MW Chitravathi pumped hydro storage project in Andhra Pradesh in FY27.
The 5 GW Maharashtra PPA execution starts from two years out, then adds 1 GW every six months per the contract.
Cumulative BESS capacity by FY30

verdicts.item: AGEL reaffirms 50 GW by 2030, targeting 85% long-term fixed PPAs and ~15% C&I plus merchant (refined to 85% PPA / 10% C&I / 5% merchant).
verdicts.note: 'firmly on course to achieve 50 gigawatt by 2030' — 50 GW reaffirmed; PPA/C&I/merchant mix not restated. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: AGEL updated strategy to include large-scale battery energy storage (BESS) deployment, primarily for RTC power and C&I customers, and will selectively participate in tenders.
verdicts.note: 'Within Khavda, we also added 1.4 gigawatt hour of battery capacity... one of the world's largest single-location battery energy storage project'; 'close to a 3 gigawatt hour... add 10 gigawatt hour o…

verdicts.item: Management confirms a battery storage strategy and plan is in place and will be disclosed at an appropriate time, evaluating adding batteries to merchant capacity.
verdicts.note: Battery storage plan now disclosed and executing: 'we are already very close to a 3 gigawatt hour... by the end of this year to add 10 gigawatt hour of storage capacities in Khavda'.

verdicts.item: AGEL maintains its ~5 GW PSP addition target by FY30-31, unaffected by the cancellation of the Kurukutty and Karrivalasa Andhra PSP projects; 1,250 MW UPPCL PSP won and 500 MW Andhra under construction.
verdicts.note: 'slated to complete our maiden 500 megawatt project at Chitravathi in Andhra Pradesh in this fiscal year' — the under-construction 500 MW progressing; 5 GW PSP / UPPCL / cancellations not restated. [±…

verdicts.item: AGEL reiterates the 50 GW by 2030 target, fully funded under its capital management framework.
verdicts.note: 'firmly on course to achieve 50 gigawatt by 2030' — target reiterated; funding framework not detailed. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management expects roughly 5 GW capacity addition again in FY27 (next year).
verdicts.note: 'we are currently planning to add 4.5 to 5.0 gigawatt of our solar and wind capacity' — FY27 ~5 GW guidance reaffirmed (slightly softened), not yet delivered. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: AGEL reaffirms the 5 GW FY26 capacity target, with ~one-third already done in Q1 and the balance ~3.5 GW to come across the next three quarters.
verdicts.note: 'we added 5.1 gigawatt' — the 5 GW FY26 capacity target was met/beaten.

verdicts.item: Chitravathi PSP execution is progressing on time; management intends it to be the earliest-commissioned PSP among peers, revenue strategy still open.
verdicts.note: 'slated to complete our maiden 500 megawatt project at Chitravathi... in this fiscal year' — on-time progress and its status as the maiden/earliest PSP confirmed.

verdicts.item: AGEL reiterates commitment to deliver 50 GW of clean power by 2030.
verdicts.note: 'achieve the goal of 50 gigawatt by 2030' — reiterated and progressing, not yet delivered. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: AGEL is well on track to complete 30 GW at Khavda by 2029; more than 4 GW operationalized there in two years.
verdicts.note: 'around 9.4 gigawatt of solar, wind, and hybrid assets already in operations' at Khavda — progressing toward 30 GW by 2029, not yet complete. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: AGEL is targeting to add 5 GW in FY26, about 150% of the prior-year addition.
verdicts.note: 'During this year, we added 5.1 gigawatt, which is 35% on a Y-o-Y growth' — met/beat the 5 GW FY26 target (though YoY growth was 35%, not the framed ~150%).

verdicts.item: Chitravathi 500 MW PSP is targeted to complete by FY27, with Tarali (1,500 MW) and Gandikota (1,800 MW) the year after, toward a 5.5 GW PSP target before the end of the decade.
verdicts.note: 'slated to complete our maiden 500 megawatt project at Chitravathi in Andhra Pradesh in this fiscal year' — Chitravathi FY27 on track; Tarali/Gandikota and 5.5 GW target not restated. [±10% rule]
